welcome_lead: Decode how TNCs structure global production.

walkthroughs.body_html: iPhone designed in California, with components from 43 countries: chips from Taiwan (TSMC), screens from South Korea (Samsung), assembled by Foxconn in Zhengzhou, China (250000 workers). Apple revenue $383 billion in 2023.

McDonald's operates in 100+ countries with 40000+ outlets. Adapts menu: McAloo Tikki (India, no beef), Teriyaki Burger (Japan), McSpaghetti (Philippines). Sources locally where possible; criticised for low wages and homogenising food culture.

TNCs create jobs (Foxconn Zhengzhou 250000), transfer technology and raise wages. Critics note race to the bottom on wages and standards. Bangladesh Rana Plaza collapse (2013) killed 1134 garment workers supplying Western TNCs.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between outsourcing and offshoring?
options: Outsourcing means contracting work to another company; offshoring means relocating work to another country. A firm can outsource without offshoring, or offshore without outsourcing (in-house overseas).
Glocalisation is a typo of globalisation.
Outsourcing and offshoring are the same thing.
Outsourcing means moving to another country and offshoring means hiring contractors.
